blockers.quote: Minus seventy-one. Two years of trash talk gave you minus six. One mock score gave you minus seventy-one. You're in his lane now. Your rival finally hates you, and you've never been prouder.
blockers.why: Check #11, Never say the feeling, fails repeatedly: this names pride, line 423 names happiness, and line 444 narrates the closing image.
blockers.fix: End line 310 with “The enemy you went looking for has finally arrived.” Replace line 423 with “And the rival is back to minus six. Between rivals, that's practically a handshake.” Start line 444 with “Your turn to be the friend. Be honest: what number would open over your head?”

blockers.quote: But here's problem two. The rival has been watching you watch the air.
blockers.why: Check #9, Earned stakes: the catch attacks the new brag-and-scan tactic, not the established habit that your best friend hears everything first.
blockers.fix: In the line 228 montage, add that your eyes seek your best friend's card first and the rival notices. Replace line 340 with “But here's problem two. Every time, you read your best friend first. The rival has been watching.”

blockers.quote: The night before, you leave your own notebook on his desk. Every mistake you made this year, and the fix. Half a chocolate bar on top. It might cost you first place. You leave it anyway. If he's building a ladder, he can have the good wood.
blockers.why: Check #22, A laugh in every scene: the notebook and exam-gate sequence is entirely earnest.
blockers.fix: Use “Half a chocolate bar on top. The bigger half. You're competitive, not a monster.” Then describe the sister arriving with “a lunch box packed like the exam lasts a week.”

suggestions.fix: Change this to the actual increasing timestamp, approximately “## [00:42] Made the Cut”; it currently follows the 00:22 chapter while moving backward.

suggestions.quote: So. Red means they want you to fail. And your list was right.
suggestions.fix: Make the thousand-card use open the next question instead of merely confirming the list: “Every red card is close. If enemies barely care and strangers don't, what is red actually measuring?”

suggestions.quote: A country holds its breath for you. Results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.
suggestions.fix: Turn the month into a choice: “For a month, every face is another chance to test the card. You don't. The next result has to come without it.”

keep.quote: Zero. Grey. One click. The biggest news of your life, and you're a receipt.
He isn't sawing your chair. He's building a ladder. Out of your mistakes. You've been his textbook for two years.
A face in a mirror is still a face. The toilets weren't broken. The one card you can't see was always yours.
